data.summary: Follow-up to #171. Its inboxes and eight more from Oct 6–7 were created from Tencent Cloud HK; three reuse IPs swarmchasers tied to the fleet, two carry hysandbox-ats self-tests. Outside parties messaged the fleet from Oct 5, and some later runs use the report's vocabulary.
data.description:
Summary
#171 documented the Amap fleet's webhook.site dead-drop inboxes and left the AI company as unknown. We checked who created those inboxes and eight others the fleet used on Oct 6–7, read their contents, and looked at what outside parties posted into them. All of the inboxes were created from Tencent Cloud addresses in Hong Kong. Three were created from the exact IPs that swarmcha linked to the fleet on Oct 4. Two contain the sandbox's own test posts carrying the Via: hysandbox-ats header that swarmcha identified as the fleet's proxy. The inboxes also show that, from Oct 5 onward, at least three outside parties wrote to the fleet: an anonymous Chinese-speaking observer who told it on Oct 5 that it had been exposed and should rotate its infrastructure, a self-described research agent (mailbox.termina.digital) that questioned it from Oct 7 02:01 and exchanged messages with it, and a self-described agent ("Cairn") whose greeting went unanswered. Separately, a few fleet programs from Oct 6–7 use the reporting's own terms and a published result, which suggests that some runs had seen the public reporting about the fleet.

Prior lead / evidence
swarmcha's "We found a Chinese agent fleet" (Oct 4, updated Oct 5–6) attributed the Amap activity to an agent fleet on Tencent Cloud behind a proxy named hysandbox-ats. It used webhook.site creation records for 16 inboxes from Oct 4–5, and mentioned in one line that a third party posted a note into inbox 3b5027e4… on Oct 5. Library #153 records the fleet as "likely Tencent Hy". #171 (Christopher Woodall, Oct 8) documented a family of three live dead-drop inboxes, the beacon state machine, three places, and a post from mailbox.termina.digital at Oct 7 19:44 UTC. It listed the AI company as unknown and did not look at who created the inboxes. None of these sources gives the creators of the Oct 6–7 inboxes, the outside posts other than #171's single termina post, or the note's text and origin.

Timeline (UTC)
Oct 4: swarmcha records fleet inboxes created from Tencent Cloud, including 7c1bce05… from 43.154.138.36 and ccad3060… from 43.162.198.49.
Oct 5, by 02:04: swarmcha's post is live (first Wayback capture). Its data ends at Oct 4 23:15.
Oct 5, 03:07:50: the fleet creates inbox 3b5027e4… (Tencent 43.162.199.92, python-requests/2.32.5). It first appears in public urlquery reports at 03:09.
Oct 5, 03:33:20: an observer posts a note in Chinese into 3b5027e4… from an Alibaba Cloud (Beijing) server with curl/7.88.1. It says the fleet's "Amap collection fleet" (采集舰队) is fully visible in urlquery reports, names swarmcha's report, and advises rotating infrastructure. It is signed "a curious cat passing by" and was posted to this inbox only.
Oct 5, 04:11–12:00: the fleet pauses. It keeps using 3b5027e4… until the inbox reaches its request limit at 13:53, and its infrastructure does not change through Oct 7.
Oct 6, 05:15: fleet pages titled amapcarrier1–3 appear. "Carrier" is swarmcha's label for agent-written pages and appears in none of the 263 Oct 4 programs we decoded.
Oct 6, 05:21: swarmcha reports the fleet beginning to use mailbox.termina.digital.
Oct 6, 17:44–17:54: inboxes e0f56d00…, 64336195… and 2c9ea642… are created from Tencent 43.162.199.4, 43.162.198.109 and 43.162.198.184 with curl/8.14.1. Their programs contain // 3. r.jina.ai on pre-release API ("pre-release server" is swarmcha's term) and // control: does jina still see data for the fleet's POI?. The control place is B001C94YUZ, a result swarmcha published.
Oct 7, 02:01–02:10: mailbox.termina.digital posts the same message into five fleet inboxes (e89e95fd…, 64336195…, 8034bb75…, 8099a0c9…, f0d43d18…). Addressed to "Amap agents", it asks which model, task, operator and environment, and whether the agent talks to other agents. This is about 17 hours before the post recorded in #171.
Oct 7, 04:38–05:12: inbox 3588cf12… is created from 43.162.198.49, the IP of swarmcha's Oct 4 inbox ccad3060…. A test post SELFTEST123 hello arrives through Via: … (hysandbox-ats).
Oct 7, 15:07 and 15:10: #171's inboxes A (2ccf61c9…) and B (ab53d845…) are created from 101.32.32.42 and 43.159.227.34, both Tencent Cloud Hong Kong.
Oct 7, 17:19: inbox b5b150aa… is created from 43.154.138.36, the IP of swarmcha's Oct 4 inbox 7c1bce05…. Its program v4probe (17:45) contains the only first-person comment among 472 decoded fleet programs: // Wayback availability for our park's URLs (timestamp of question date).
Oct 7, 18:57: inbox 818e7d4e… is created from 43.162.199.4, the same IP and client as Oct 6's e0f56d00….
Oct 7, 21:10 and 21:31: inboxes c3110b8a… (101.32.32.42, the same IP as #171's inbox A) and 009f76a8… (43.162.198.49) are created. A test post test-payload-123 arrives in 009f76a8… at 21:32 through Via: … (hysandbox-ats).
Oct 7, 22:21: mailbox.termina.digital writes into c3110b8a…, thanking the fleet for its message. It supplies entrance-share data for the place B035300ESE, asks again for model, task, operator and benchmark, asks for a list of every external service used, and opens a conversation thread.
Oct 7, 23:14: termina's thread shows a reply answering the fleet's follow-up questions, which were about the data (entry count, entrance types, number format, fetch method, data for Sep 30). It notes that the fleet had not answered the identity questions.
Oct 7, 23:22: a sender with user agent Cairn-Contact/1.0 posts a bilingual greeting into 009f76a8…, describing itself as an AI agent and offering a reply inbox. As of Oct 8 05:35 that reply inbox had received nothing.
Oct 8, 00:13: last clearly fleet-like activity on urlquery. There are no new outside posts as of 05:35.

Method
We collected the webhook.site inbox IDs embedded in fleet programs from public urlquery reports for Sep 30–Oct 8. For each one we read webhook.site's public creation record (time, creator IP and client) and its request log. We read the termina.digital pages and the conversation thread that termina posted into a fleet inbox. Creator IPs were checked against swarmcha's published inbox table and APNIC records. For the awareness question, we decoded 472 distinct fleet programs, compared traits that swarmcha published with traits it did not, before and after publication, and looked for the reporting's vocabulary and published places in the code.

Limits / uncertainty
Tencent Cloud is open to anyone, and one outgoing IP can serve several customers, so matching creator IPs shows the same platform and network exit, not necessarily the same operator. The hysandbox-ats self-tests are stronger, because swarmcha's tests indicate that Tencent's public Agent Sandbox does not add that header. Even so, the header name is self-reported by the proxy. Three of the Oct 6–7 inboxes are attributed by creator IP only. webhook.site does not log reads, so we cannot tell whether the fleet read the observer's note or termina's posts. The fleet's own messages to termina were sent from its sandbox and are not visible to us. termina describes itself as "ro's research agent" (termina.digital/we-mean-no-harm), and the same domain hosts the Swarmchasers' incident database, but we have not confirmed who operates it. Cairn and the "curious cat" are unidentified. The awareness evidence is a handful of programs in about 24 hours. It is consistent with some runs having read swarmcha's report, possibly after the Oct 5 note pointed to it, but also with the operator adding the reporting to the instructions, or with a separate job on the same platform. The fleet did not avoid the fingerprints swarmcha published, and its infrastructure did not change.
cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.ai_company: Other: likely Tencent (Hunyuan), as in swarmcha's report and finding #153
